description: The clean run with the AP-1 text in CRLF bytes and the config declaring the published text's hash, 48e7826f…. The AP-1 text is hashed as it is on disk, not with its line endings made LF as the other text inputs are (T3-50), because it must be the publisher's deposit byte for byte: the CRLF copy hashes to 6ecd964a…, so the seal is refused before any request, naming both hashes. A runner that made the AP-1 text's line endings LF before hashing would seal it. A CRLF copy declared with its own hash is refused by the AP-1 version check after the seal, which this harness cannot express; tests/functional/test_step4_g5_seal_verifier.py::test_run_crlf_copy_of_the_v13_text_with_its_own_hash_refused covers it.
exercises: the AP-1 text hashed as raw bytes (T3-50)
scratch_copy: Runs in a scratch copy: the CRLF AP-1 text is made there, at the sealed default path, which in the real tree is a tracked LF file.
